test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Pankaj, Meera, and Ashok invest ₹41,000, ₹39,000, and ₹84,000 respectively to start a business. At the end of the year, the total profit earned is ₹49,200. 29% of the total profit earned is given to charity and the rest is divided among them in the ratio of their investments. What will be the share of Ashok (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Investment ratio **Pankaj : Meera : Ashok** = 41 : 39 : 84 (Sum of parts = 164).

Total profit = ₹49,200. Remaining profit after 29% charity = 71% of 49,200.

Ashok share = (84 ÷ 164) × 0.71 × 49,200.

Ashok share = 84 × 0.71 × 300 = 84 × 213 = ₹17,892.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,892.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Investments: **Pankaj** = ₹41,000, **Meera** = ₹39,000, **Ashok** = ₹84,000. Total Profit = ₹49,200. Charity = 29%.
Formulas: Profit Share Ratio = Investment Ratio × Time | Share = (Individual Ratio ÷ Total Ratio) × Distributed Profit.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/27a6513a57f967aca2df7cc019becbc2e9c1d58c7d702ee09e5560b76cab3b7d.png] 
⇒ **Remaining Profit** = 49,200 − (29 ÷ 100 × 49,200) = 49,200 − 14,268 = ₹34,932.
⇒ **Ratio of investments** = 41,000 : 39,000 : 84,000 = 41 : 39 : 84.
⇒ **Sum of ratios** = 41 + 39 + 84 = 164 units.
⇒ 164 units = ₹34,932 ⇒ 1 unit = 34,932 ÷ 164 = ₹213.
⇒ **Ashok share** (84 units) = 84 × 213 = ₹17,892.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,892.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Basics

When time periods are the same, the **profit sharing ratio** is directly proportional to the **investment ratio**.

Handling Charity/Tax

Always subtract the non-distributable amount (Charity, Tax, Reserves) from the **Gross Profit** to find the **Net Distributable Profit**.
